identity.title: Capture recipe bytes once for execution provenance

origin.kind: scheduled 2D task execution and source review
origin.summary: The 2D plan identified separate recipe deserialization, byte hashing, and text reads as a provenance race. The scheduled cycle authorized a bounded fix that keeps one captured byte generation as the execution and provenance source.

state.current_summary: VisionRecipeRunner now reads a recipe file once into bytes, deserializes the same bytes, and passes them into VisionPipelineExecutionPlan. SerializeHelper supports byte-backed XML deserialization, including BOM-aware UTF-8 and UTF-16, while the execution plan hashes and retains those exact original bytes. Focused Debug/Release contracts and solution builds pass.

claims.text: The file-based VisionRecipeRunner path previously deserialized a recipe and then read the same path again for bytes and text, allowing provenance to describe a different file generation under replacement.

problem.impact: A result could pair execution from one recipe generation with a hash or XML snapshot from another, weakening reproducibility and review evidence.

criteria.text: The file-based Runner captures recipe bytes exactly once, does not perform a second text read or file deserialization, and deserializes from the captured bytes.
UTF-8 BOM, UTF-8 non-BOM, and UTF-16 recipe bytes deserialize correctly; the execution plan retains the exact original bytes and its original SHA-256 equals those bytes for both A and B generations.
Invalid XML bytes and an invalid recipe file fail before pipeline execution rather than producing a result.
OpenVisionLab and VisionRecipeRunnerSmoke build cleanly in Debug and Release, and existing cancellation, failure-lifetime, and finite-acceptance regression contracts remain passing.
The change keeps the existing recipe XML format, execution owner, result contract, and SDK/DLL provenance boundary unchanged.

context.location: VisionPipelineExecutionPlan stores the original byte snapshot and writes OriginalPipelineSha256 into VisionPipelineExecutionProvenance; VisionRecipeRunResult projects those existing fields.

artifacts.summary: Debug/Release app and smoke builds, six-case recipe snapshot contracts, full solution builds, and cancellation/failure-lifetime/finite-acceptance regression logs.

evidence.observation: The file overload contains one File.ReadAllBytes(recipeXmlPath) capture, passes those bytes to SerializeHelper.TryLoadFromXmlBytes, and no longer calls File.ReadAllText(recipeXmlPath) or TryLoadFromXmlFile(recipeXmlPath). The execution plan uses byte-backed deserialization when text is absent and retains the same bytes for hashing and result provenance. The source contract passed the one-read/static ownership assertions.

The focused recipe-file-snapshot contract passed 6/0 in Debug and Release. It covered one-read source ownership, UTF-8 BOM/non-BOM, UTF-16, exact original bytes and SHA-256, and sequential A/B generation identity/provenance pairing.
The contract rejected malformed XML bytes and an invalid recipe file before execution, retaining a load error and producing no run result.

OpenVisionLab and VisionRecipeRunnerSmoke Debug/Release builds plus full solution Debug/Release builds completed with exit code 0, warnings 0, and errors 0. Existing cancellation passed 5/0, failure-lifetime passed 7/0, and finite-acceptance passed 10/0 in both configurations.

events.summary: The one-read byte snapshot owner, encoding-aware deserialization, exact provenance hash, invalid-input fail-closed behavior, focused contracts, and Debug/Release regression gates are complete. Full RC distribution verification remains the separate PL-0061 blocked boundary.
